title: Local finite presentation under a ring-object isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab)$ with the sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Let $\varphi:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be an isomorphism of ring objects. Use module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], finite presentations [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], and local finite presentations [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] preserves and reflects local finite presentation. More precisely, for every $S$-module $N$, a pro-étale covering family witnesses local finite presentation of $N$ if and only if the same family witnesses it for $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N$; the finite presentation ranks can be kept unchanged. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ preserves and reflects local finite presentation of $R$-modules, with the same covers and ranks.

source.place: Proof: "such that each $M|_{U_a}$ is locally finitely presented" and the restriction calculations; justify relabelling local finite presentations across the canonical coefficient-ring isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $\psi=\varphi^{-1}$. The sheaf tensor structure is symmetric and closed, and tensoring preserves colimits [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]; the small-site convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] lets [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification] apply with coefficients $\Ab$, giving an abelian sheaf category. By [def-sp-abelian], equalizers are kernels of differences and coequalizers are cokernels of differences, so both exist. Thus clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] applies to both $\varphi$ and $\psi$: $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}$. Their restriction functors are quasi-inverse. In fact double restriction restores the action: $\gamma_N\circ(\varphi\otimes1)\circ(\psi\otimes1)=\gamma_N$ and similarly for an $R$-module. The comparison maps have underlying identity. A presentation is unchanged in ranks when its last isomorphism is composed with an isomorphism of modules, directly from [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: clause 5 in both directions; inverse-action identity expanded by the agent

proof.text: Suppose $N\cong\operatorname{coker}(S^m\xrightarrow{a}S^n)$. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-extension-finite-presentation] to $\psi:S\to R$. It supplies $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}N\cong\operatorname{coker}(R^m\xrightarrow{a_R}R^n)$, with $a_R$ the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}(a)$. Compose with the component $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}N\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N$ from step 1. This is the required presentation of the restriction, with exactly $m,n$. Conversely, given a presentation of $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N$ with ranks $m,n$, apply the same cited lemma to $\varphi$ and compose $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N\cong N$. The inverse-action calculation of step 1 supplies the last isomorphism. This proves both directions for finite presentations, on any scheme, without a flatness assumption.

source.place: local presentations on strata; expanded using inverse scalar extension

proof.text: Fix any pro-étale covering family $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}$, and set $F_i=u_i^*$ and $\varphi_i=F_i\varphi$. These pullbacks are strong monoidal [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]. They are moreover symmetric monoidal, so $F_iR$ and $F_iS$ are commutative ring objects of $\Sh(U_{i,\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab)$ [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], as step 2 on $U_i$ requires. Also $F_i\psi$ is inverse to $\varphi_i$, since functoriality sends $\varphi\psi=1$ and $\psi\varphi=1$ to the same identities. In [def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square] take $F=F_i$, $R_Y=F_iR$, $S_Y=F_iS$, $\eta_R=1$, $\eta_S=1$, and $\varphi_Y=F_i\varphi$. Its square commutes identically and its comparison gives $\operatorname{mapMod}(F_i)(\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_i}(\operatorname{mapMod}(F_i)N)$. Apply step 2 on the scheme $U_i$, then compose presentation isomorphisms with this comparison. Thus for each $i$ finite presentations on the two sides exist with exactly the same pair $(m_i,n_i)$. By [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] this very family witnesses local finite presentation on one side if and only if it does on the other. No refinement or change of indices has occurred.

source.place: same covering witnesses for locally finitely presented restrictions; monoidal square comparison

proof.text: For an $R$-module $M$, clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] identifies $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M$ with $\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}M$. Apply step 3 to the isomorphism $\psi:S\to R$. For each fixed cover and each member, applying $\operatorname{mapMod}(u_i^*)$ to this module isomorphism again gives an isomorphism, since any functor sends mutually inverse maps to mutually inverse maps. Composing the cokernel-presentation isomorphisms with these maps leaves both ranks unchanged [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Hence that cover, with any specified presentation ranks, works for $M$ exactly when it works for $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M$. This proves the extension clause, including reflection.

source.place: coefficient relabelling of local presentations; extension clause

tool_uses.why: Generic existence of the abelian category of sheaves with Grothendieck abelian coefficients; needed only to check equalizers and coequalizers for scalar change.

Generic finite-free cokernel calculation under any scalar extension, including unchanged ranks. The present unit has no such algebraic calculation; this is a tool for coefficient relabelling, not a replacement of its constructibility route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q108-4cdad9e58 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item (statement unchanged, 4 steps, no new nodes), the statement of every cited node, the parent lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves and its main-20261015 proof. The parent uses the extension clause (Ext along the invertible alpha_g preserves and reflects local finite presentation, same covers), which is exactly what the item states. Step 1: clause 5 of sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars applies to phi and to psi=phi^-1. Its hypotheses come from the symmetric closed sheaf tensor that preserves colimits on both sides, and from the abelian sheaf category (lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification, def-sp-abelian). The directions are right: Ext_psi = Res_phi, and Res_psi Res_phi = id. Step 2: the statement of lem-sfb-internal-extension-finite-presentation gives the same ranks m,n, used in both directions. Step 3: def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square with eta=1 gives mapMod(u_i^*) Res_phi = Res_{u_i^*phi} mapMod(u_i^*), and the cover and ranks are unchanged. Step 4 is an elementary assembly. Edge cases checked: phi=id, zero rings, m or n zero, empty cover. No duplicate in the DAG, no cycle, no SGA. All three kinds of Mathlib search are recorded. The two declared tool_uses are in units on the item's route and are accepted. FIX (C1/E1): step 3 applies step 2 on U_i, which needs u_i^*R and u_i^*S commutative, and strong monoidality alone does not give that.
